TCS-0001.reason: The central boundary between efficiently solving a problem and efficiently checking a proposed solution; consequences span nearly all of TCS.

TCS-0002.reason: Tests whether efficient certificates exist symmetrically for yes and no answers, with broad implications for complexity and proof systems.

TCS-0003.reason: Asks whether polynomial-time randomness can always be eliminated, a foundational computational-model comparison.

TCS-0004.reason: A basic deterministic-versus-nondeterministic space question, captured by directed reachability.

TCS-0005.reason: A central algebraic complexity separation with broad consequences for arithmetic computation and polynomial families.

TCS-0006.reason: A major organizing conjecture for approximation thresholds and the limits of efficient optimization.

TCS-0007.reason: The exponent of matrix multiplication governs a fundamental algebraic primitive and the running times of many other algorithms.

TCS-0008.reason: Asks whether linear programming admits a running time independent of coefficient bit length in the strongly polynomial sense; a central optimization-model gap.

TCS-0009.reason: A concrete explicit arithmetic lower-bound target that tests the strength of current algebraic complexity techniques.

TCS-0010.reason: Superlinear explicit arithmetic lower bounds would break a basic barrier in understanding the cost of polynomial computation.

TCS-0011.reason: A central existence question for a strong and widely studied fairness guarantee for indivisible goods.

TCS-0012.reason: Connects worst-case hardness to typical-case hardness, a foundational gap affecting algorithms and cryptography.

TCS-0013.reason: Efficient explicit tree codes would give a fundamental construction for reliable interactive communication.

TCS-0014.reason: A sharply defined monotone formula lower-bound target for a basic Boolean function; informative but narrower than unrestricted circuit barriers.

TCS-0016.reason: Strong circuit lower bounds for SAT would establish a sweeping limitation on nonuniform efficient computation.

TCS-0017.reason: A structural conjecture about formula composition that could turn local lower bounds into stronger general formula lower bounds.

TCS-0018.reason: Tests whether two-sided efficiently checkable evidence guarantees efficient computation, with relevance to total search and cryptographic candidates.

TCS-0019.reason: Separates computation with reuse from formula computation, a basic structural distinction in circuit complexity.

TCS-0020.reason: Tests the power of polynomial-size nonuniform computation against exponential-time computation, a central circuit lower-bound question.

TCS-0021.reason: Nonuniform circuits for NP probe a foundational hardness boundary even stronger than the uniform P-versus-NP separation.

TCS-0022.reason: Asks whether worst-case NP hardness suffices for one-way functions, directly connecting complexity theory to the existence of cryptography.

TCS-0023.reason: Efficiently learning DNF is a central computational learning benchmark whose structure recurs across learning models.

TCS-0024.reason: Would connect circuit hardness with the power of propositional proof systems, transferring progress between two difficult lower-bound areas.

TCS-0025.reason: Superpolynomial Frege lower bounds are a central barrier in propositional proof complexity.

TCS-0026.reason: Tests whether randomness helps space-bounded computation, a fundamental counterpart to polynomial-time derandomization.

TCS-0027.reason: A basic quantum transformation problem under black-box access, clarifying what an oracle interface permits.

TCS-0028.reason: Separates two quantum oracle access conventions, a precise model question whose scope is narrower than general quantum speedups.

TCS-0029.reason: Determines the strongest quantum query advantage when the function has no promise, a basic limit on quantum computation.

TCS-0030.reason: An oracle benchmark for the reach of efficient-prover interactive verification of quantum computation.

TCS-0031.reason: A model-relative separation probing the relation between quantum computation and classical interactive proofs.

TCS-0032.reason: A concrete test of whether a celebrated quantum traversal advantage extends to producing an entire path.

TCS-0033.reason: Relates quantum query algorithms to polynomial approximation, connecting two core tools for quantum upper and lower bounds.

TCS-0034.reason: Characterizes simultaneous time and memory limits for basic quantum collision tasks, beyond query complexity alone.

TCS-0035.reason: A specific sampling benchmark that can clarify the computational meaning of cross-entropy performance.

TCS-0036.reason: Asks whether quantum polynomial-time computation is more powerful than randomized classical computation.

TCS-0037.reason: Tests whether quantum computation can efficiently solve every efficiently verifiable search-decision problem.
